# Index of modules

The task guides, every registry kind, then every module of the engine and its tools: what it is for (its file
comment's first sentence), what it exports and the tests that cover it. Each export, with the first sentence of its
doc comment, is in [API.md](API.md); error and advice codes are in [ERRORS.md](ERRORS.md).

## Start here

The task guides, as AGENTS.md lists them under "Where things are", and the skills: read each when the task needs
it.

- [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](../docs/PROGRESS.md): read first, every session: where things stand, what is next, the open issues.
- [`docs/TESTING.md`](../docs/TESTING.md): the tiers, and which unit tests and specs a change selects.
- [`labs/box/README.md`](../labs/box/README.md): the box's scenes, settings and quick loop; adding a scene or a variant (a variant is a new scene file or a settings preset, never a change of meaning in a passing scene).
- [`tests/replays/README.md`](../tests/replays/README.md): the replay format; checking, recording and making replays.
- [`tools/templates/`](../tools/templates/): `node x new <kind> <id>` writes a module, scene, material… from its kind's template and checks it (`node x new` lists the kinds).
- [`.claude/skills/`](../.claude/skills/): the skills, each loaded when its description says (x-loop after any change, stress-box for the box, determinism-debugging when hashes part, rapier, three-webgpu, escalation).
  - [`.claude/skills/determinism-debugging/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/determinism-debugging/SKILL.md): How to find and fix a determinism bug in my-3dge. Use whenever x replay, a replay test or a hash comparison fails.
  - [`.claude/skills/escalation/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/escalation/SKILL.md): When and how to escalate to the owner in my-3dge. Use before any such action, and when the SessionStart hook or the Stop hook names an open escalation.
  - [`.claude/skills/rapier/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/rapier/SKILL.md): Rapier physics in my-3dge under the reproducibility contract. Use when adding bodies, colliders or queries, touching engine/physics, or debugging a physics hash or capture.
  - [`.claude/skills/stress-box/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/stress-box/SKILL.md): The Stress Box (labs/box), the engine's integration target. Use when you work on the box, add or tune a box scene, or need to show an engine capability in the box.
  - [`.claude/skills/three-webgpu/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/three-webgpu/SKILL.md): Writing three.js code in my-3dge. Use before writing, reviewing or debugging code that imports three.js.
  - [`.claude/skills/x-loop/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/x-loop/SKILL.md): The my-3dge work loop, edit → check → test → report. Use whenever you change code in this repository, or are unsure what to run next.

## Kinds

Every registry kind (PLAN.md §6.6), from its `defineKind` call: `node x describe <kind>` lists its fields and ids.

| Kind              | What it is                                                                                                                                                               | Declared in                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `actionMap`       | Named actions and the physical codes bound to each (keys by KeyboardEvent.code, mouse, pad by position): what the input devices turn into intents.                       | [`engine/input/actionMaps.ts`](../engine/input/actionMaps.ts)             |
| `body`            | Puppet bodies: parts on the humanoid skeleton, one line each, with material slots (the palette).                                                                         | [`engine/gfx/puppets/grammar.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/grammar.ts)       |
| `build`           | Body proportions for the humanoid skeleton, in metres before size (limbs, torso, head, stance, gait).                                                                    | [`engine/anim/builds.ts`](../engine/anim/builds.ts)                       |
| `component`       | Component kinds: the plain-object data entities hold (e.position), with their fields. The canonical state and the hash read every component's declared fields, in order. | [`engine/sim/state.ts`](../engine/sim/state.ts)                           |
| `feature`         | Optional GPU features and techniques: what each needs, what is lost without it, and its advice code.                                                                     | [`engine/gfx/features.ts`](../engine/gfx/features.ts)                     |
| `geometry`        | Shapes props, levels and bodies name by id: a builder of a three.js BufferGeometry with its parameters and a vertex budget.                                              | [`engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts)   |
| `glyph`           | Level legend glyphs: what one map character means (heights, floor shape, solid, collider and mesh recipes, nav flags, spawn, light spot, surface, footprint).            | [`engine/world/level/glyph.ts`](../engine/world/level/glyph.ts)           |
| `inspectorMember` | Members of the inspector (__engine, createHeadless): a call or property with its help line, argument schema and implementation.                                          | [`engine/dev/members.ts`](../engine/dev/members.ts)                       |
| `level`           | Levels: a level text (front matter and a map in legend characters) that compileLevel turns into data.                                                                    | [`engine/world/level/level.ts`](../engine/world/level/level.ts)           |
| `light`           | What a level's light spot shines with: three.js's PointLight parameters, its priority in the light pool and its flicker.                                                 | [`engine/gfx/lights.ts`](../engine/gfx/lights.ts)                         |
| `material`        | Materials as data with three.js's classic parameters (color, map, roughness, emissive, flags); the engine decides how to draw them.                                      | [`engine/gfx/materials/material.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/material.ts) |
| `prop`            | Props: things that stand in a level, as data: meshes (geometry and material by id), a body, an optional light spot, where a level places them, and interaction hooks.    | [`engine/world/props/prop.ts`](../engine/world/props/prop.ts)             |
| `scene`           | Scenes: a level, settings, a setup and a step, sim-side, so x sim, x replay and createHeadless run them in Node.                                                         | [`engine/sim/scene.ts`](../engine/sim/scene.ts)                           |
| `setting`         | The engine's and the game's settings, by dotted path: one schema for x set, URL parameters and __engine.set.                                                             | [`engine/core/settings.ts`](../engine/core/settings.ts)                   |
| `sfx`             | A sound effect: voices for the DSP core, layers of other effects, variants and a mixer bus.                                                                              | [`engine/audio/data/sfx.ts`](../engine/audio/data/sfx.ts)                 |
| `sky`             | Sky presets: what surrounds and lights a level (background, dome, backdrop, sun, ambient light, fog, how bright the point lights shine).                                 | [`engine/gfx/sky.ts`](../engine/gfx/sky.ts)                               |
| `song`            | A looping tune in tracker notation: tempo, bars and tracks of notes or drum tokens.                                                                                      | [`engine/audio/data/song.ts`](../engine/audio/data/song.ts)               |
| `texture`         | Seeded, periodic texture generators: colour, height, roughness and emissive per texel, with their parameters, size, tile, density and look.                              | [`engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts)     |
| `touchlayout`     | A page's touch controls: the buttons in the corner fan, each pressing an action, and whether the menu button shows.                                                      | [`engine/ui/touch.ts`](../engine/ui/touch.ts)                             |

## The root

- [`eslint.config.js`](../eslint.config.js): ESLint's settings for T0 (PLAN.md §6.10; `npm run lint`, inside `npm run check`): typescript-eslint's recommended rules without type information (so T0 stays fast), the file-comment and size rules, then the doctrine's rule families from tools/eslint/, one block per family, each message naming the fix.
  - Exports: `configure`, `default`, `SWITCHES`
- [`playwright.config.ts`](../playwright.config.ts): Playwright Test's settings for T2 (PLAN.md §6.10, §8.8): one project, `webgpu`, on the platform's Chromium with shardfall's WebGPU flags, against a Vite dev server it starts itself.
  - Exports: `default`
- [`vite.config.ts`](../vite.config.ts): Vite's settings (the dev server and the build) and Vitest's (T1), in one file as Vitest expects (PLAN.md §6.10, WPs 0.2 and 0.12).
  - Exports: `default`
  - Tests: [`tools/lib/vite.test.ts`](../tools/lib/vite.test.ts)

## engine/anim

- [`authoring.ts`](../engine/anim/authoring.ts): Effector-space authoring (PLAN.md WP 3.6, ADR-0009, Appendix C): a pose is written as targets in the character's own terms and solved onto the rotation skeleton.
  - Exports: `B`, `fromFRU`, `fru`, `FRU`, `holdAlong`, `LimbSide`, `Rig`, `rigFromWorld`, `rigToWorld`, `Sided`, `SIDES`, `sideSign`, `SOLVE`, `solveArm`, `solveLeg`, `solveSpine`, `SpineTargets`, `turnRight`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/authoring.test.ts`](../engine/anim/authoring.test.ts)
- [`blob.ts`](../engine/anim/blob.ts): The blob rig (PLAN.md WP 5.3): my-3d2dge's `Blob`, the squash-and-stretch ball of slimes, jellies and bats, on a minimal skeleton.
  - Exports: `Blob`, `BLOB`, `BLOB_JOINTS`, `BLOB_LEAP`, `BLOB_MOVES`, `BlobInput`, `BlobJoint`, `BlobLeap`, `blobMove`, `BlobMove`, `BlobMoveFrame`, `BlobMoveName`, `blobMoveTimes`, `BlobOptions`, `BlobPose`, `BlobState`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/blob.test.ts`](../engine/anim/blob.test.ts)
- [`builds.ts`](../engine/anim/builds.ts): Body builds (PLAN.md WP 3.4, §5.2, I-08): the registry kind `build`, one entry per body proportion set, in metres.
  - Exports: `Build`, `BUILD_FIELDS`, `buildKind`, `BuildSpec`, `defineBuild`, `getBuild`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/builds.test.ts`](../engine/anim/builds.test.ts)
- [`character.ts`](../engine/anim/character.ts): The character animator (PLAN.md WP 3.7, §6.4, ADR-0009; I-09): `Animator` drives a body (the procedural humanoid, engine/anim/humanoid.ts) through an explicit, named layer stack, keeps its sockets, samples its trail (socket history), reports its footsteps and returns all of it as plain JSON (`inspect()`).
  - Exports: `Animator`, `ANIMATOR_FIELDS`, `AnimatorData`, `AnimatorOptions`, `AnimatorPool`, `AnimatorReport`, `AnimEvent`, `CHARACTER_CODES`, `FOOTSTEP`, `PoseOptions`, `TRAIL`, `TrailSample`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/character.test.ts`](../engine/anim/character.test.ts)
- [`check.ts`](../engine/anim/check.ts): The core of `anim.check(def)` (PLAN.md WP 3.4): `animCheck` runs a set of poses through FK and reports what breaks the body's contract, as plain sentences: values that are not finite, bones that changed length, declared rigid pairs that drifted, feet below the floor, and sockets out of reach.
  - Exports: `animCheck`, `AnimCheckName`, `AnimCheckReport`, `AnimCheckSpec`, `AnimProblem`, `CHECK_CODES`, `PointName`, `RigidPair`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/check.test.ts`](../engine/anim/check.test.ts)
- [`fk.ts`](../engine/anim/fk.ts): Forward kinematics (PLAN.md WP 3.4, I-08): `forwardKinematics(skeleton, pose)` turns a pose's local rotations into each joint's world matrix, position and rotation, and the helpers read a joint, a socket or a leaf bone's tip out of the result as three.js math objects.
  - Exports: `createWorldPose`, `forwardKinematics`, `jointMatrix`, `jointPosition`, `jointRotation`, `jointToWorld`, `socketPosition`, `tipPosition`, `WorldPose`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/fk.test.ts`](../engine/anim/fk.test.ts)
- [`floater.ts`](../engine/anim/floater.ts): The floater rig (PLAN.md WP 5.3): a hovering body (wisps, ghosts, drones) that banks into its turns, with motes orbiting it.
  - Exports: `Floater`, `FLOATER`, `FloaterInput`, `FloaterOptions`, `FloaterPose`, `FloaterState`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/floater.test.ts`](../engine/anim/floater.test.ts)
- [`humanoid.ts`](../engine/anim/humanoid.ts): The procedural humanoid (PLAN.md WP 3.6, §5.2; I-09): my-3d2dge's `Humanoid` on the rotation skeleton.
  - Exports: `Humanoid`, `HumanoidInput`, `HumanoidOptions`, `HumanoidState`, `KNOCKDOWN`, `STEP`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/humanoid.test.ts`](../engine/anim/humanoid.test.ts)
- [`ik.ts`](../engine/anim/ik.ts): Inverse kinematics for the humanoid skeleton (PLAN.md WP 3.5, I-11): `twoBone` (my-3d2dge's `ik3`) places a limb's middle joint, `twoBoneRot` turns a leg or an arm to a target with a pole, `aim` spreads a look-at over chest, neck and head within limits, `footPlant` stands the feet on probed ground, and `handTo` puts a grip in a hand.
  - Exports: `aim`, `AIM_CHAIN`, `AimLink`, `AimOptions`, `createFootPlantState`, `FOOT_PLANT`, `FootLock`, `footPlant`, `FootPlantOptions`, `FootPlantState`, `GroundHit`, `GroundProbe`, `handTo`, `IK_CODES`, `Limb`, `LimbEnd`, `LIMBS`, `twoBone`, `TwoBoneOptions`, `twoBoneRot`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/ik.test.ts`](../engine/anim/ik.test.ts)
- [`locomotion.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion.ts): Procedural locomotion for the humanoid (PLAN.md WP 3.6, §5.2): my-3d2dge's gait, idle, lean and arm-swing formulas as effector targets in the character's own terms (`B(f, r, u)`, authoring.ts): where the pelvis rides, where each foot and hand swings, which way the spine and the head lean, where the shoulders sit.
  - Exports: `BodyMotion`, `crouchShare`, `EffectorContext`, `GAIT`, `gaitFoot`, `gaitHand`, `headDirection`, `hipTarget`, `HumanoidWeights`, `pelvisTarget`, `restContext`, `shoulderTarget`, `spineDirection`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/poses.test.ts`](../engine/anim/poses.test.ts)
- [`pose.ts`](../engine/anim/pose.ts): Poses (PLAN.md WP 3.4, I-08, I-49): `Pose` holds a root transform and one local rotation per joint of the humanoid skeleton; `blendPoses` crossfades two (slerp or nlerp) under a bone mask, `makeAdditive` and `addPose` make and apply additive layers, and `hashPose` digests one.
  - Exports: `addPose`, `BlendOptions`, `blendPoses`, `hashPose`, `JointRef`, `makeAdditive`, `Pose`, `POSE_LENGTH`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/pose.test.ts`](../engine/anim/pose.test.ts)
- [`poses.ts`](../engine/anim/poses.ts): Held poses, stances and the humanoid's effector layers (PLAN.md WP 3.6, §5.2; I-09): the names a humanoid takes (`POSES`, `STANCES`, `WEAPONS`), with a warning that suggests the closest name for a misspelt one, and the ordered tables that lay each pose, stance and state over the gait's targets: `FOOT_LAYERS` for the soles, `HAND_LAYERS` for the wrists, `BLADE_LAYERS` for the weapon's direction.
  - Exports: `applyLayers`, `BLADE_LAYERS`, `createEffectors`, `DROPPED_BLADE`, `EffectorLayer`, `Effectors`, `effectorStage`, `FOOT_LAYERS`, `HAND_LAYERS`, `layerWeights`, `Placement`, `POSE_CODES`, `poseName`, `PoseName`, `POSES`, `stanceName`, `StanceName`, `STANCES`, `Weapon`, `weaponName`, `WEAPONS`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/poses.test.ts`](../engine/anim/poses.test.ts)
- [`sheet.ts`](../engine/anim/sheet.ts): Skeleton contact sheets (PLAN.md WP 3.4, `anim.sheet()`): `animSheet(frames)` draws poses as stick figures in one SVG, in Node, each frame from the views asked for, so an agent can look at a pose, a move's samples or a state matrix without a browser.
  - Exports: `animSheet`, `Sheet`, `SHEET_VIEWS`, `SheetFrame`, `SheetOptions`, `SheetView`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/sheet.test.ts`](../engine/anim/sheet.test.ts)
- [`skeleton.ts`](../engine/anim/skeleton.ts): The humanoid skeleton (PLAN.md WP 3.4, §5.2, Appendix C; I-01, I-08): a root plus 23 joints, their sockets, the rest pose a build gives them (`createSkeleton`), and bone masks (`boneMask`) for blending.

## engine/app

- [`animMember.ts`](../engine/app/animMember.ts): The inspector member `anim(id?)` (PLAN.md §8.3; WP 3.7's member, delivered at gate G3's review): an animated actor's character animator as `Animator.inspect()` gives it (engine/anim/character.ts): its weights, each slot of the layer stack with what is active in it, the effectors, sockets, events and trail.
  - Tests: [`engine/app/viewMembers.test.ts`](../engine/app/viewMembers.test.ts), [`labs/box/scenes/room-hero.test.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/room-hero.test.ts)
- [`engine.ts`](../engine/app/engine.ts): The engine in a page (PLAN.md §6.4, §6.9, §8.3, WP 2.7): `createEngine({ canvas, scenes, levels })` registers the levels the page imported as text, reads the page's routes (engine/app/routes.ts: `?scene ?seed ?cam ?replay` and settings by path), starts the scene as a recorded run with its view (engine/app/headless.ts, engine/app/view.ts), publishes the run's inspector as `window.__engine`, starts the renderer (WebGPU or nothing, engine/gfx/renderer.ts), warms up every pipeline the view needs through both cameras (perspective and orthographic), draws the first frame, and then runs the frame loop (engine/app/loop.ts): the devices sampled into intents (engine/input/input.ts; `__engine.input` drives the same session), fixed steps from the clock, the view drawn at the clock's alpha.
  - Exports: `createEngine`, `Engine`, `ENGINE_CODES`, `EngineOptions`, `recordOf`
  - Tests: [`engine/app/engine.test.ts`](../engine/app/engine.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/box.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/box.spec.ts)
- [`feelMember.ts`](../engine/app/feelMember.ts): The inspector member `feel(id?)` (PLAN.md §8.3, WP 3.2): an actor's feel meter report, `measureFeel` (engine/sim/actors.ts) over the actor's character at the run's rate and `physics.characterGravity`; the first player when `id` is absent, else `SIM_BAD_ARGUMENT` naming the actors' ids (`none` in a scene without one).
  - Tests: [`engine/app/viewMembers.test.ts`](../engine/app/viewMembers.test.ts), [`engine/sim/actors.test.ts`](../engine/sim/actors.test.ts)
- [`headless.ts`](../engine/app/headless.ts): The engine without a page (PLAN.md §8.3, §6.9, WPs 1.6 and 2.7; doctrine: Verifiable): `createHeadless({ scene, seed, settings, view })` starts a scene as a recorded session (engine/sim/scene.ts) and returns its inspector, the same object a page publishes as `window.__engine` minus a renderer: `render` and `shot` throw `DEV_NO_RENDERER`.
  - Exports: `AppHostOptions`, `AppRun`, `createAppHost`, `createHeadless`, `Drawing`, `Headless`, `HEADLESS_CODES`, `headlessHost`, `HeadlessOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/app/headless.test.ts`](../engine/app/headless.test.ts)
- [`loop.ts`](../engine/app/loop.ts): The frame loop (PLAN.md §6.4, WP 2.7; doctrine: Reproducible): fixed sim steps plus interpolation, once per animation frame.
  - Exports: `createLoop`, `FRAME_SLACK_MS`, `FRAME_SLOT_MS`, `Loop`, `LoopOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/app/loop.test.ts`](../engine/app/loop.test.ts)
- [`playback.ts`](../engine/app/playback.ts): Replays one step at a time (PLAN.md §6.5 item 9, §6.7's CPU-only contract, WP 2.7): what lets a page render between the steps of a replay, so `x replay --browser page` and tests/e2e/parity.spec.ts prove that rendering never changes play, and `?replay=<name>` plays one in real time.
  - Exports: `createPlayback`, `Playback`, `PLAYBACK_CODES`, `playInto`, `PlayIntoOptions`, `PlayResult`, `PlayTarget`, `ViewChange`

- [`routes.ts`](../engine/app/routes.ts): Routes and deep links (PLAN.md §6.1: URL parameters are parsed once, here, and passed down; §8.1; WP 2.7): what a page's query asks for.

  - Tests: [`engine/app/routes.test.ts`](../engine/app/routes.test.ts)
- [`view.ts`](../engine/app/view.ts): The view of a run (PLAN.md §6.4's `view.update`, §8.3, WP 2.7): what a running scene looks like, built without a GPU, so a page draws it and `createHeadless({ view: true })` dumps it in Node.

## engine/audio/dsp

- [`biquad.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/biquad.ts): Biquad filters of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): the eight types of Web Audio's `BiquadFilterNode` (lowpass, highpass, bandpass, notch, allpass, peaking, lowshelf, highshelf), with the coefficients of Robert Bristow-Johnson's Audio EQ Cookbook, which Web Audio's own formulas come from.
  - Exports: `Biquad`, `FILTER_TYPES`, `FilterType`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/biquad.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/biquad.test.ts)
- [`delay.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/delay.ts): The delay (echo) effect of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): a feedback delay line, as a `DelayNode` looped through a feedback `GainNode` and mixed back with the dry signal is in Web Audio.
  - Exports: `echo`, `ECHO_FLOOR`, `echoCount`, `echoSpacing`, `EchoSpec`, `MAX_ECHOES`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/delay.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/delay.test.ts)
- [`envelope.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/envelope.ts): Volume envelopes of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): the source's percussive envelope (a linear attack, then an exponential fall to 0.0005 at the end, as Web Audio's `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` gives it) and ADSR (attack, decay, sustain, release), which also covers the source's `hold` (sustain at full volume, a 30 ms release).
  - Exports: `AdsrEnvelope`, `Envelope`, `envelopeCurve`, `FALL_FLOOR`, `FallEnvelope`, `holdEnvelope`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/envelope.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/envelope.test.ts)
- [`measure.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/measure.ts): Numbers about rendered samples (PLAN.md WP 9.1, §8.5; doctrine: Verifiable without a display): peak, RMS, DC offset and the amplitude of one frequency (Goertzel's algorithm), so tests and tools judge a sound by numbers instead of by ear.
  - Exports: `dcOffset`, `peak`, `rms`, `toneAmplitude`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/measure.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/measure.test.ts)
- [`osc.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/osc.ts): The tonal oscillators of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1; doctrine: Quality under the hood): square, pulse 25%, pulse 12.5%, triangle, sine and saw, each a function of a phase.
  - Exports: `blamp`, `blep`, `DUTY`, `oscillate`, `TONAL_WAVES`, `TonalWave`, `wrap`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/osc.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/osc.test.ts)
- [`pluck.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/pluck.ts): The Karplus–Strong pluck of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): a burst of seeded noise circulating in a delay line whose loop averages neighbouring samples, so it rings like a plucked string and darkens as it decays.
  - Exports: `Pluck`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/pluck.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/pluck.test.ts)
- [`render.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.ts): The DSP core's entry point (PLAN.md WP 9.1, §6.5, ADR-0013; doctrines: Assets, Reproducible, Verifiable): `render(def, seed, rate)` turns a sound definition (engine/audio/dsp/voice.ts) into a `Float32Array` of mono samples, and `soundHash` digests one, so every sound is code, renders in Node, and checks by its hash.
  - Exports: `DEFAULT_RATE`, `render`, `RENDER_CODES`, `soundHash`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/audio-dsp.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/audio-dsp.spec.ts)
- [`synth.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/synth.ts): One voice rendered into samples (PLAN.md WP 9.1): the pitch path (an exponential sweep, the arpeggio's steps, vibrato), the source (a tonal oscillator with optional FM, seeded white noise, or a Karplus–Strong pluck), the filter, the envelope and the echo, in that order, added into the sound's buffer at the voice's start.
  - Exports: `renderVoice`, `voiceEnd`, `voiceSamples`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts)
- [`voice.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/voice.ts): A sound definition and its checks (PLAN.md WP 9.1; doctrines: Assets, Agent-operable): a sound is plain data, one voice or a list of voices played together, in the source chip synth's words (`wave`, `freq`, `to`, `dur`, `vol`, `attack`, `hold`, `arp`, `step`, `loop`, `vib`, `filter`, `q`), so its effects, drums and songs copy over as they are (WP 9.2), plus ADSR (`decay`, `sustain`, `release`), a start time `at`, an explicit filter, `fm`, `pluck` and a `delay` echo.
  - Exports: `DelaySpec`, `FilterSpec`, `FmSpec`, `MAX_SECONDS`, `normalizeSound`, `NormalVoice`, `noteFreq`, `Pitch`, `PluckSpec`, `SoundDef`, `Voice`, `VOICE_CODES`, `Wave`, `WAVES`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts)

## engine/audio/runtime

  - Exports: `loopLayout`, `passSamples`, `renderLayers`, `SongLayer`, `songLayers`, `toBuffer`

  - Tests: [`engine/audio/runtime/voices.test.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/voices.test.ts)

## engine/gfx/geometry

- [`box.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/box.ts): Boxes (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `boxGeometry({ width, height, depth })`, three.js's `BoxGeometry` with two changes the level meshes and props need: it stands on the ground (its bottom at y 0, centred in X and Z), and its UVs are in metres, so a texture keeps its density (16 texels per metre for the v1 textures) on every face whatever the box's size, instead of being stretched over each face.
  - Exports: `boxGeometry`, `BoxOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`builtins.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/builtins.ts): The geometry kit's built-in entries (PLAN.md WP 2.4): one `geometry` entry per builder of engine/gfx/geometry/, its parameters the builder's options as schema fields with the builder's defaults, and a vertex budget a little above what the defaults build.
  - Exports: `BUILT_IN_GEOMETRY`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts)
- [`checks.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/checks.ts): The geometry kit's codes and argument checks (PLAN.md WP 2.4): a builder given sizes it cannot build (a size of 0, a limb shorter than the difference of its radii, a ring whose inner radius is not below its outer) throws `GFX_BAD_GEOMETRY`, naming the shape, the problem and what to pass, before it writes a vertex.
  - Exports: `assertSegments`, `assertSizes`, `badGeometry`, `GEOMETRY_CODES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`frustum.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/frustum.ts): Frustums, prisms and cylinders (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `frustumGeometry({ radiusBottom, radiusTop, height, radialSegments, smooth })`, three.js's `CylinderGeometry` standing on the ground, with UVs in metres: an octagonal dais, a brazier's bowl, a barrel, a cone (`radiusTop` 0), a well.
  - Exports: `frustumGeometry`, `FrustumOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`geometry.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts): The geometry registry (PLAN.md WP 2.4, §6.6, I-29): the registry kind `geometry`, one entry per shape a prop, a level or a body names by id (§6.1: `world` names geometry by id, `gfx` builds it).
  - Exports: `buildGeometry`, `defineGeometry`, `GEOMETRY_FIELDS`, `GeometryEntry`, `geometryKind`, `GeometryRef`, `GeometrySpec`, `getGeometry`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts)
- [`groups.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/groups.ts): Draw groups and merging (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `sidesThenTops(geometry)` sorts a geometry's triangles into two draw groups, its sides (material 0) then its tops and bottoms (material 1), so a box, a pillar or a wall drawn with a face material and a top material costs two draw calls instead of one per face; `mergeGeometries` joins indexed geometries with the same attributes into one.
  - Exports: `mergeGeometries`, `sidesThenTops`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`inspect.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/inspect.ts): Geometry measured as numbers (PLAN.md WP 2.4, §8.6, I-29): `inspectGeometry(geometry)` counts what the `geo` QA family (tools/qa/geo.ts) and the kit's tests check, in Node: vertices and triangles, missing attributes (`position`, `normal`, `uv`), index entries out of range, NaN or infinite numbers, degenerate triangles (an area below 1e-10 m²: a sliver no pixel shows, which breaks normals and physics hulls), normals that are not of length 1 (within 1e-3), triangles wound against their own normals (a corner's normal pointing away from the side the winding faces: the face is culled where it should show, or lit from behind), and the bounds.
  - Exports: `DEGENERATE_AREA`, `GeometryReport`, `inspectGeometry`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`limb.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/limb.ts): Tapered limbs (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `limbGeometry({ length, radiusStart, radiusEnd })`, the smooth hull of two spheres, one of `radiusStart` at the origin (the joint) and one of `radiusEnd` at `length` up +Y (the next joint): an upper arm, a thigh, a finger, a tail segment.
  - Exports: `limbGeometry`, `LimbOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`pillar.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/pillar.ts): Pillar parts (PLAN.md WP 2.4): the prototype's pillar, a plinth, a shaft of dressed stone and a capital of two slabs, as sizes (`pillarParts`) and as one geometry (`pillarGeometry`: the parts' boxes merged, sides then tops, so a pillar is two draw calls however many stand).
  - Exports: `pillarGeometry`, `PillarOptions`, `PillarPart`, `pillarParts`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`ramp.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/ramp.ts): Ramps and wedges (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `rampGeometry({ width, depth, low, high })`, a block standing on the ground whose top slopes from `low` at its -Z end up to `high` at its +Z end, so walking forward (+Z, the way characters face) climbs it.
  - Exports: `rampGeometry`, `RampOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`ring.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/ring.ts): Rings (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `ringGeometry({ innerRadius, outerRadius, height, radialSegments })`, a ring lying on the ground around the Y axis.
  - Exports: `ringGeometry`, `RingOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`roundedBox.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/roundedBox.ts): Rounded boxes (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `roundedBoxGeometry({ width, height, depth, radius, segments })`, a box whose edges and corners are rounded with `radius`, as three.js's `RoundedBoxGeometry` addon draws one, standing on the ground like every shape of the kit (its bottom at y 0, centred in X and Z), with UVs in metres and smooth normals.
  - Exports: `roundedBoxGeometry`, `RoundedBoxOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`writer.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/writer.ts): The geometry writer (PLAN.md WP 2.4): the one place the kit's builders (engine/gfx/geometry/) turn vertices and triangles into a three.js `BufferGeometry` with `position`, `normal` and `uv` and an index.
  - Exports: `createWriter`, `cross`, `dot`, `normalize`, `ProfilePoint`, `Vec3`, `Writer`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)

## engine/gfx/level

- [`brazier.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/brazier.ts): Brazier stands (PLAN.md WP 4.4): `brazierGeometry(level, pieces, bottom, top)` draws a stone foot and a bowl of glowing coals on each piece of a brazier glyph, sized to the glyph's `radius` (its cylinder collider) and its height, and lays the ground under the pieces' tiles (the floor, another glyph, has none there).
  - Exports: `brazierGeometry`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts)
- [`cells.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/cells.ts): Level cells and the way they face out (PLAN.md WP 2.4): one cell per piece of a block mesh (a wall tile, a pillar's footprint), with its tiles, its centre, its size and its outward direction, the way it faces out of the room, away from the open floor beside it.
  - Exports: `LevelCell`, `levelCells`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts)
- [`dais.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/dais.ts): Daises (PLAN.md WP 4.4): `daisGeometry(tile, daises, pieces, ground)` draws each dais (engine/world/level/ types.ts, `DaisDescriptor`) as its octagonal frustum, built on the very corners of its hull collider (`frustumPoints`, engine/world/level/shapes.ts), so what is drawn is where feet stand: the sloped edge (and an upright skirt below it when the dais stands above the ground) and the flat octagonal top.
  - Exports: `daisGeometry`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts)
- [`faces.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/faces.ts): Faces for the level's shapes (PLAN.md WP 4.4): what the stairs, gallery, dais and brazier builders (engine/gfx/level/{stairs,slab,dais,brazier}.ts) write their faces with.
  - Exports: `Ground`, `polygon`, `slotted`, `Slotted`, `tread`, `upright`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts)
- [`meshes.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/meshes.ts): The level meshes (PLAN.md WP 2.4, WP 4.4, §6.1 "data descriptors"): `createLevelMeshes(level, { materials })` draws a compiled level (engine/world/level/compile.ts) from its mesh descriptors: one mesh per descriptor, built in the shape of the recipe its glyphs name (engine/gfx/level/recipes.ts, shapes.ts).
  - Exports: `createLevelMeshes`, `LEVEL_MESH_CODES`, `LevelMeshes`, `LevelMeshesOptions`, `LevelMeshPart`, `meshDrawCalls`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/hall.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/hall.spec.ts), [`tests/e2e/level-meshes.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/level-meshes.spec.ts)
- [`recipes.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/recipes.ts): Level mesh recipes (PLAN.md WP 2.4, WP 4.4): how the level meshes (engine/gfx/level/meshes.ts) draw the tiles of a glyph whose `mesh` names a recipe (engine/world/level/legend.ts).
  - Exports: `CutWhen`, `FALLBACK_RECIPE`, `LEVEL_RECIPES`, `LevelCut`, `LevelRecipe`, `LevelShape`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts), [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts)
- [`shapes.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.ts): The level's shapes (PLAN.md WP 2.4, WP 4.4): `buildShape(level, descriptor, recipe, materials)` builds the mesh of one mesh descriptor (engine/world/level/types.ts) in its recipe's shape (engine/gfx/level/recipes.ts): a welded surface (the floor), instanced blocks (walls, low walls) or pillars (plinth, shaft and capital, engine/gfx/geometry/pillar.ts), or one mesh for a slab (a gallery, slab.ts), the stairs (stairs.ts), a dais (dais.ts) or brazier stands (brazier.ts).
  - Exports: `buildShape`, `BuiltShape`, `instanced`, `PartCut`, `placeInstances`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts), [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts)
- [`slab.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/slab.ts): Slabs (PLAN.md WP 4.4): `slabGeometry(tile, pieces, bottom, top)` draws a raised block of tiles as one solid, a gallery: its walk, one welded surface over every tile at `top` (engine/gfx/level/surface.ts), and its sides, upright faces from `bottom` to `top` along the outline only, where a piece's tile meets a tile that is not one of the pieces' (or the map's edge).
  - Exports: `slabGeometry`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts)
- [`stairs.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/stairs.ts): Stairs (PLAN.md WP 4.4): `stairsGeometry(tile, ramps, ground)` draws each ramp (engine/world/level/types.ts, `RampDescriptor`) as a flight of steps standing on the ground at height `ground`: `stepsOf(ramp)` steps, two per metre of run, rising evenly from the ramp's bottom to its top toward the side it `rises` to.
  - Exports: `stairsGeometry`, `STEP_RUN`, `stepsOf`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.test.ts)
- [`surface.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/surface.ts): Level surfaces (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `surfaceGeometry(tile, pieces, y)` lays one flat surface over a level's pieces at height `y`, facing up: the floor.

  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/meshes.test.ts)

## engine/gfx/textures

- [`bake.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts): The CPU bake (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §6.7, I-20): runs a texture generator (engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts) over every texel and returns its maps as plain typed arrays, named as three.js's material slots name them: `map` (the colour, sRGB RGBA bytes), `heightMap` and `roughnessMap` (floats 0–1), `emissiveMap` (sRGB RGBA bytes, or null when nothing glows) and `normalMap` (tangent-space RGBA bytes, from the height).
  - Exports: `bakeKey`, `BakeSource`, `bakeTexture`, `newTexel`, `normalsFromHeight`, `TextureBake`, `TextureRef`, `textureSampler`, `TextureSampler`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/bake.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/bake.test.ts)
- [`codes.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/codes.ts): The texture codes (PLAN.md WP 2.3): the errors a bake raises for a size its pattern cannot tile at or a palette with no colours, each naming its fix (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
  - Exports: `TEXTURE_CODES`
- [`dataTexture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.ts): A bake as three.js textures (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §6.7): `toDataTextures` turns a CPU bake (engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts) into `DataTexture`s for a material's slots, `map`, `normalMap`, `roughnessMap` and `emissiveMap`, each with its full mip chain computed on the CPU (engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts), repeating, and filtered for the look: `pixel` magnifies with nearest (crisp texels) and minifies with nearest texels blended between levels (no shimmer at a distance), `smooth` filters linearly on both, with 4× anisotropy for floors seen at a grazing angle.
  - Exports: `DataTextureOptions`, `TextureMaps`, `toDataTextures`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.test.ts)
- [`mips.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts): Mipmaps on the CPU (PLAN.md WP 2.3, I-20): the full chain of a baked map down to 1 × 1, each level an area-weighted box filter of the one above, computed in the right space for what the map holds.
  - Exports: `linearToSrgbByte`, `mipChain`, `mipCount`, `MipEncoding`, `MipLevel`, `SRGB_TO_LINEAR`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/mips.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/mips.test.ts)
- [`seams.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/seams.ts): Texture quality measures (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §8.6, I-20): what the `tex` QA family (tools/qa/tex.ts) and the unit tests check a bake against.

## engine/gfx/textures/generators

- [`brick.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/brick.ts): The brick generator (`texture:brick`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): brick courses in running bond, each brick its own tone, a mortar joint along each course's bottom and each brick's right, a lit top row on every brick, and dark specks.

- [`flagstone.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/flagstone.ts): The flagstone generator (`texture:flagstone`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): square stones in running-bond rows, each its own tone from the palette, with a one-texel joint along its left and top, a lit bevel inside the joint and a shaded one along its bottom and right (light from the top left, as pixel art paints it), specks of grit, and a crack across some stones.
  - Exports: `FLAGSTONE`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`planks.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/planks.ts): The plank generator (`texture:planks`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): floor boards running along x, a dark gap along the bottom of each board and at each board's end (the ends staggered per row), each board its own tone, and grain: streaks long along the board and short across it.

  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`staves.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/staves.ts): The barrel-stave generator (`texture:staves`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): staves running up, each its own tone and a dark gap along its right edge, the odd knot, and iron hoops across them (a lit top row, a shaded one under it), for a barrel's side wrapped round a cylinder (x round, y up).

  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`stone.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/stone.ts): The dressed-stone generator (`texture:stone`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): big blocks in running bond, bevelled (lit top and left, dark bottom and right) with a joint along the bottom and right, each block its own tone, worn patches from noise.
  - Exports: `STONE`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)

- [`props.ts`](../tests/pages/props.ts): The props page's module (tests/pages/props.html, PLAN.md WP 4.5): the engine's four props in a walled yard on the engine's renderer, standing in Rapier, drawn by engine/gfx/props.ts.

- [`puppets.ts`](../tests/pages/puppets.ts): The puppets page's module (tests/pages/puppets.html, PLAN.md WP 3.8): the engine's renderer with a lit scene (a hemisphere light and one shadow-casting sun: one shadow map) and four things to show, one at a time, each registered with the warm-up before the first frame: - the neutral humanoid (`body:humanoid`, build:chibi) as one rigid-skinned puppet (engine/gfx/puppets/draw.ts), in the page's test pose (`testPose`: every joint turned up to 0.5 rad about a seeded axis, the root turned 0.6 rad); - the socket marks (fixtures/bodies/socketMarks.ts) in the same build and pose, as a puppet of their own; - a crowd of instanced humanoids (`createPuppetBatches`) with blob shadows, on a grid 1.5 m apart, each in a seeded pose of its own; - the fixture body `body:everyPart` (fixtures/bodies/everyPart.ts), one part of every type, in the same build: one rigid-skinned puppet and two instanced ones of its own batches (`parts/…`), one facing the camera and one turned away (its cape), so every part type is drawn both ways.

- [`replay.ts`](../tests/pages/replay.ts): The replay page's module (`tests/pages/replay.html`), Chromium's half of `node x replay --browser sim` (PLAN.md §6.5 item 9, WP 1.5): the sim in a page with no renderer.
- [`scene.ts`](../tests/pages/scene.ts): The scene page's module (tests/pages/scene.html): the fixture scene (tests/pages/sceneFixture.ts) drawn by the engine's renderer (engine/gfx/renderer.ts) for the render tests, which drive it through `window.__scene` and import the modules they test into the page (`await import('/engine/gfx/pipelines.ts')`): the same module instances the page runs.
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/renderer.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/renderer.spec.ts)
- [`sceneFixture.ts`](../tests/pages/sceneFixture.ts): The scene page's fixture (tests/pages/scene.html): a small scene as plain data, and `buildScene`, which turns a description into three.js objects.
  - Exports: `buildScene`, `BuiltScene`, `FIXTURE`, `LightSpec`, `MaterialSpec`, `MeshSpec`, `PoolSpec`, `SceneDescription`, `ShapeSpec`
- [`shot.ts`](../tests/pages/shot.ts): The shot page's module (tests/pages/shot.html): a fixture scene made for the ID pass and the look metrics, drawn by the engine's renderer (engine/gfx/renderer.ts), and `window.__engine` with `ready`, `errors`, `info()` and `shot(options)`: engine/gfx/shot.ts's `shot`, returned as JSON through `shotForJson`, the member `x shot` calls (WP 2.7 registers the engine's own, §8.3).
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/shot.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/shot.spec.ts)

## tools/eslint

- [`askTheEntry.ts`](../tools/eslint/askTheEntry.ts): The local rule "ask the entry, never the id" (PLAN.md §6.6, ADR-0012): shared code reads an entry's hooks and fields, each with a default on the kind's schema, and never compares a registered id, so new content works without editing the code that uses it.
  - Exports: `default`, `ID_SHAPE`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/askTheEntry.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/askTheEntry.test.ts)
- [`banned.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.ts): The banned and renamed three.js APIs (PLAN.md Appendix B; doctrine: Mastery), scoped by path, each message naming the replacement: legacy and fragile APIs, names from releases newer than the pinned r182, r182's deprecations (any deprecation warning fails a test anyway), and GPU readbacks outside the two files allowed them.
  - Exports: `BANNED_FILES`, `BANNED_IMPORT_FILES`, `bannedBlocks`, `bannedPlugin`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/banned.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.test.ts)
- [`family.ts`](../tools/eslint/family.ts): Plumbing for the rule families of eslint.config.js: core rules re-exposed under a family's own name, and per-path zones for bans that have exceptions.
  - Exports: `Ban`, `family`, `messagesOf`, `resolvingImports`, `shortest`, `zoned`
- [`index.ts`](../tools/eslint/index.ts): The local ESLint plugin and the rule families eslint.config.js assembles (PLAN.md §6.1, §6.5, §6.10, Appendix B): one module per family, each exporting its blocks, and `local`, the plugin for what no stock rule expresses.
  - Exports: `askTheEntryBlocks`, `bannedBlocks`, `family`, `layerBlocks`, `local`, `publicApiBlocks`, `simSideBlocks`
- [`layers.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.ts): The layer rules (PLAN.md §6.1; doctrines: WebGPU only, Reproducible): one `no-restricted-imports` block per engine layer, naming what the layer may import, so a forbidden edge fails T0 with the rule and the way round it.
  - Exports: `layerBlocks`, `layerPlugin`, `THREE_MATH`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/layers.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.test.ts)
- [`namespaceNames.ts`](../tools/eslint/namespaceNames.ts): `banned/no-namespace-names` (PLAN.md Appendix B, WP 1.6): a banned three.js name read off a namespace of its entry point, however the namespace is named or the name is spelt.
  - Exports: `EntryName`, `namespaceNames`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/banned.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.test.ts)
- [`publicApi.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.ts): The public-API rule (PLAN.md §6.1, ADR-0020; doctrine: Quality under the hood): game code imports the engine only through its barrels, `engine/index.ts` (pages) and `engine/sim-api.ts` (sim-side code), and never three.js or Rapier directly, so game agents never depend on, or need to read, the internals.
  - Exports: `publicApiBlocks`, `publicApiPlugin`, `SIM_SIDE_GAME_CODE`, `unnamedImports`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/publicApi.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.test.ts)
- [`simSide.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.ts): The reproducibility bans for sim-side code (PLAN.md §6.5, Appendix B; doctrine: Reproducible): no clocks, no unseeded randomness, no DOM, no Web Audio, no three.js, so identical inputs and seeds give identical play in Node and in Chromium.
  - Exports: `SIM_SIDE`, `simPlugin`, `simSideBlocks`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/simSide.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.test.ts)
- [`testing.ts`](../tools/eslint/testing.ts): Lints fixtures for the ESLint tests (WP 0.4): writes each source at its repository path inside a temporary directory and lints it through ESLint's Node API with eslint.config.js's own `configure(…)`, so every rule is proved by a failing and a passing fixture, and nothing failing is ever committed.
  - Exports: `ALL_ON`, `Case`, `caseProblems`, `CaseResult`, `ConfigModule`, `describeMessages`, `lintCases`, `lintFixtures`, `loadConfigModule`, `Switches`, `uncovered`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/config.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/config.test.ts)

## tools/lib

- [`browser.ts`](../tools/lib/browser.ts): Chromium for the tools and the e2e fixture, through Playwright: the launch options `playwright.config.ts` also uses, the init script every page gets before its own scripts run (a virtual clock, seeded randomness and a WebGPU probe), and page errors mapped to `.ts` files and lines through Vite's inline source maps (§8.1, §8.8).
  - Exports: `AdapterRecord`, `browserRuntime`, `cachedChromium`, `CHROMIUM_VERSION`, `chromiumPath`, `ConsoleRecord`, `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM`, `describePageError`, `GpuLog`, `initScript`, `launchBrowser`, `launchOptions`, `mapPageError`, `mapStack`, `PageError`, `PageWatch`, `parseStack`, `preparePage`, `servedPath`, `SourceFrame`, `VIEWPORT`, `VirtualClock`, `WEBGPU_FLAGS`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/harness.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/harness.spec.ts), [`tools/lib/browser.test.ts`](../tools/lib/browser.test.ts)
- [`deps.ts`](../tools/lib/deps.ts): The dependency record (`tools/deps.json`) and the model behind `x deps` (PLAN.md §6.10, doctrine: Mastery): versions and their lines, the 12-month rule, registry answers, and the lockfile's types packages.
  - Exports: `compareVersions`, `DepsRecord`, `evenLines`, `firstOfNextLine`, `gitBlob`, `isDay`, `isRelease`, `Knowledge`, `lineName`, `lineOf`, `LockEntry`, `Lockfile`, `lookup`, `newestInLine`, `newestQualified`, `NextLine`, `parseVersion`, `PinRecord`, `qualifiesOn`, `readRepository`, `RECORD`, `RegistryAnswer`, `Release`, `Repository`, `Rule`, `RULES`, `satisfies`, `SECTIONS`, `stableReleases`, `todayUtc`, `TYPES`, `TypesDep`, `typesInLock`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/deps.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/deps.test.ts), [`tools/lib/deps.test.ts`](../tools/lib/deps.test.ts)
- [`depsCheck.ts`](../tools/lib/depsCheck.ts): The offline dependency check: package.json, the lockfile, `.nvmrc` and the pinned docs against `tools/deps.json` (PLAN.md §6.10).
  - Exports: `checkDeps`, `CheckDepsOptions`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/deps.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/deps.test.ts)
- [`depsUpdate.ts`](../tools/lib/depsUpdate.ts): The network half of `x deps` (PLAN.md §6.10): `--update` adopts each pin's newest compatible release and rewrites `tools/deps.json`; `--qualify` lists the lines that have qualified beyond the pins, as upgrade WPs.
  - Exports: `Adoption`, `NETWORK`, `NetworkOptions`, `planUpdate`, `Qualified`, `qualify`, `Registry`, `Runner`, `SPAWN`, `update`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/deps.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/deps.test.ts)
- [`docs.ts`](../tools/lib/docs.ts): Reads the manual out of the code (PLAN.md §6.8, WP 0.6): each module's file comment, its exports with their doc comments, its `@example` blocks, its tests, the codes it registers and the registry kinds it declares, through the TypeScript compiler API.
  - Exports: `directoryOf`, `DocComment`, `DocTag`, `Example`, `ExportDoc`, `isModulePath`, `lineOf`, `listModules`, `MODULE_ROOTS`, `ModuleDoc`, `parse`, `parseDocComment`, `readModule`, `readModules`, `ResolvedExport`, `resolveExports`, `resolveSpecifier`, `walk`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`docsCodes.ts`](../tools/lib/docsCodes.ts): Reads the error and advice codes a module registers with `defineCodes` (PLAN.md WP 1.2, §6.8): `x docs` collects them into `docs/ERRORS.md` and fails a code without its fix.
  - Exports: `CodeDoc`, `codesOf`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`docsExamples.ts`](../tools/lib/docsExamples.ts): Runs the `@example` blocks of file and export comments in Node (PLAN.md §8.12, WP 0.6): `x docs --check` runs them, and so does `tests/unit/examples.test.ts` in T1.
  - Exports: `collectExamples`, `compileExample`, `EXAMPLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ExampleOutcome`, `rewriteImports`, `runExample`, `runExamples`
  - Tests: [`tests/unit/examples.test.ts`](../tests/unit/examples.test.ts), [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`docsGenerate.ts`](../tools/lib/docsGenerate.ts): Writes the generated docs from what tools/lib/docs.ts reads (PLAN.md §6.8, WP 0.6): `docs/INDEX.md` (the "Start here" task guides and skills of tools/lib/docsStart.ts, a row per registry kind declared with `defineKind`, PLAN.md §6.6, then module → purpose → exports → tests), `docs/API.md` (each export with the first sentence of its doc comment, the public API first) and `docs/ERRORS.md` (every code registered with `defineCodes`, with its message and fix).
  - Exports: `apiMarkdown`, `BARRELS`, `errorsMarkdown`, `formatMarkdown`, `GENERATED`, `generateDocs`, `indexMarkdown`, `kindRows`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`docsHelp.ts`](../tools/lib/docsHelp.ts): The `help()` drift check (PLAN.md §8.12, §8.3, WP 1.6; doctrine: Agent-operable): `x docs --check` fails when the inspector's `help()` differs from its real API, the members the object actually has.
  - Exports: `apiOf`, `checkHelp`, `helpDrift`, `helpNames`, `memberModules`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`docsKinds.ts`](../tools/lib/docsKinds.ts): Reads the registry kinds a module declares with `defineKind` (PLAN.md §6.6, WP 1.2): `x docs` gives each kind its row in `docs/INDEX.md` (kind, description, declaring module) and fails a declaration it cannot read, so the index of kinds is never written by hand.
  - Exports: `KindDoc`, `kindsOf`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`docsPaths.ts`](../tools/lib/docsPaths.ts): The path checks of `x docs` (PLAN.md §8.12, WP 0.6): every path, source citation and name that the file and export comments, AGENTS.md, README.md and the Markdown under `docs/` mention must exist.
  - Exports: `checkable`, `checkPaths`, `coveredDocs`, `expand`, `GENERATED_DIRS`, `isPlanned`, `PathOptions`, `Planned`, `readPlanned`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`docsStart.ts`](../tools/lib/docsStart.ts): The "Start here" section that opens `docs/INDEX.md` (PLAN.md §6.8): the task guides AGENTS.md lists under "Where things are", then every skill in `.claude/skills/`, with its description's headline and the sentence that says when to load it.
  - Exports: `Guide`, `Skill`, `skills`, `SKILLS`, `startHere`, `taskGuides`, `whenToLoad`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/docs.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.test.ts)
- [`escalations.ts`](../tools/lib/escalations.ts): Escalation records (DOCTRINE.md, Escalation; PLAN.md §8.14, ADR-0017): `docs/escalations/ESC-NNNN-<slug>.md`, front matter then a short body.
  - Exports: `canonicalPrinciple`, `deadlineFor`, `DIR`, `Escalation`, `FIELDS`, `generateIndex`, `INDEX`, `indexMarkdown`, `isoSeconds`, `isOverdue`, `nextId`, `parseRecord`, `PRINCIPLES`, `readRecords`, `RecordFile`, `serializeRecord`, `slugOf`, `Status`, `STATUSES`, `validateFields`, `WAIT_MINUTES`, `wellFormed`, `writeIndex`, `writeRecord`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/esc.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/esc.test.ts)
- [`filmCompare.ts`](../tools/lib/filmCompare.ts): The frame comparison of `x film` (tools/cmd/film.ts, PLAN.md WP 3.11): `compareFrames` compares a filmed frame with the base's pixel by pixel and gives each differing pixel to an object through the ID pass, `judgeCompare` turns a film's differences into its verdict and findings, and `checkFilmThumbs` holds each frame's thumbnail to `tests/baselines/thumbs/<case>.json`.
  - Exports: `checkFilmThumbs`, `compareFilmThumbs`, `compareFrames`, `EMPTY`, `FilmFrame`, `FilmObject`, `FilmVerdict`, `FrameDiff`, `judgeCompare`, `samePixel`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/film.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/film.test.ts)
- [`filmSheet.ts`](../tools/lib/filmSheet.ts): The contact sheet of `x film` (tools/cmd/film.ts, PLAN.md WP 3.11): frames laid out in columns, each labelled in a 3 × 5 pixel font drawn in Node (no canvas, no font file), with the base's frames and a diff row (A in grey, each differing pixel in magenta) when the film was compared.
  - Exports: `contactSheet`, `drawText`, `LABEL`, `MAGENTA`, `Sheet`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/film.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/film.test.ts)
- [`hash.ts`](../tools/lib/hash.ts): The FNV-1a hash (32-bit), shared by the tools: report ids, the e2e fixture's named random streams, and the proof hashes later WPs print.
  - Exports: `fnv1a`, `fnv1aHex`
  - Tests: [`tools/lib/hash.test.ts`](../tools/lib/hash.test.ts)
- [`page.ts`](../tools/lib/page.ts): Pages for the `x` commands (PLAN.md §8.1, §8.3, WP 2.7): reading a page's ready-or-error signal (`window.__engine`), waiting for it, finding the page that draws a scene module's scenes, and playing replays in that page, opened on each replay's scene, for `x replay --browser page` (`pageRuntime`: `__engine.replay`, engine/app/playback.ts, which draws a frame after every step), or in tests/pages/replay.html for `--browser sim` (`replayBrowser`).
  - Exports: `BrowserMode`, `labPageOf`, `PageEngine`, `pageRuntime`, `readSignals`, `READY_MS`, `replayBrowser`, `scenePath`, `Signals`, `waitReady`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/inspect.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/inspect.test.ts)
- [`png.ts`](../tools/lib/png.ts): Decodes the PNGs Chromium's screenshots produce (non-interlaced, 8-bit RGB or RGBA) into RGBA bytes, for the frame reads of the e2e fixture (tests/e2e/fixtures.ts) and `x shot` (tools/cmd/shot.ts).
  - Exports: `decodePng`
  - Tests: [`tools/lib/png.test.ts`](../tools/lib/png.test.ts)

- [`source.ts`](../tools/lib/source.ts): The read-only source checkouts: my-3d2dge at `$MY3D2DGE_SRC` and shardfall at `$SHARDFALL_SRC` (PLAN.md WP 0.1).

  - Tests: [`tools/lib/vite.test.ts`](../tools/lib/vite.test.ts)

## tools/qa

- [`audio.ts`](../tools/qa/audio.ts): The `audio` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 9.4, I-23, I-29): `node x qa audio` renders every sound the shared registry has, the engine's `sfx` and `song` entries (engine/audio/data) and a game's (each `*.ts` module under `labs/<name>/sounds/` imported first), and measures each render by numbers: no ear needed (doctrine: Verifiable).
  - Exports: `AUDIO_LIMITS`, `checkSounds`, `dbfs`, `default`, `fft`, `findClicks`, `frameSpectrum`, `loadSoundModules`, `soundMetrics`, `SoundMetrics`, `soundModules`, `SoundProblem`, `soundProblems`, `spectralCentroid`
  - Tests: [`tools/qa/audio.test.ts`](../tools/qa/audio.test.ts)
- [`geo.ts`](../tools/qa/geo.ts): The `geo` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 2.4, I-29): `node x qa geo` checks every `geometry` entry the shared registry has (the kit's, engine/gfx/geometry/builtins.ts, and a game's: each `*.ts` module under `labs/<name>/geometry/` imported first), built at its defaults; every `prop` entry's parts (WP 4.5: the engine's, engine/world/props/catalog.ts, and a game's under `labs/<name>/props/`), each built as the prop draws it, under the prop's id; and the level meshes (engine/gfx/level/meshes.ts) of every level file the `level` family reads (tools/qa/level.ts: `labs/box/levels/`, `fixtures/levels/`; a level that does not compile is the `level` family's to report).
  - Exports: `checkGeometries`, `checkLevelMeshes`, `checkProps`, `default`, `geometryModules`, `labModules`, `LEVEL_DRAW_CALLS`, `LEVEL_VERTICES_PER_TILE`, `MAX_SIZE`, `PROP_FLOAT`
  - Tests: [`tools/qa/geo.test.ts`](../tools/qa/geo.test.ts)
- [`level.ts`](../tools/qa/level.ts): The `level` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 2.2, I-29): `node x qa level` validates every level file, the box's (`labs/box/levels/*.txt`, ids `level:<name>`) and the fixtures' (`fixtures/levels/*.txt`, ids `level:fixtures/<name>`; the seeded errors under `fixtures/levels/broken/` are the unit tests' business and are skipped), and runs in T1 through `runQa` (tools/qa/level.test.ts).
  - Exports: `default`, `LEVEL_DIRS`, `LevelFile`, `levelFiles`
  - Tests: [`tools/qa/level.test.ts`](../tools/qa/level.test.ts)
- [`tex.ts`](../tools/qa/tex.ts): The `tex` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 2.3, I-20): `node x qa tex` bakes every texture generator the shared registry has, the engine's (engine/gfx/textures/v1.ts) and a game's (each `*.ts` module under `labs/<name>/textures/` imported first), at its default size and at twice it, with seeds 1 and 2, and checks every bake; then, under each `prop` entry's id (WP 4.5; a game's props under `labs/<name>/props/` imported first), the textures its parts' materials name, baked as each material bakes them (its parameters and size), and a `reference` violation for a part naming a material no entry defines.
  - Exports: `checkPropTextures`, `checkTextures`, `default`, `textureModules`
  - Tests: [`tools/qa/tex.test.ts`](../tools/qa/tex.test.ts)
